capture.supports: 10-second wrist-acceleration windows and participant-isolated validation. 10 seconds exceeds this harness limit.

capture_augment.supports: Time warp sigma .05, knots 4, probability 1; magnitude warp sigma .05, knots 2, probability 1. Upstream also shifts windows; that shift is not used here.

tinier_normalize.supports: Standardization and min-max normalization implementations; min-max is a candidate, not the training default.

paper.supports: Benchmark architecture families, dataset scope and source-only selection. Does not disclose an exact initial pipeline per dataset.

adaptations: 10-second source windows are adapted to the protected maximum of 5 seconds; no sequence smoothing or upstream shift augmentation is claimed.
Neural architectures are the supplied benchmark families, not the CAPTURE-24 authors’ CNN/RNN implementations.
No fitted normalization is the primary candidate; source-only min-max is a separately evaluated adaptation.
Warp mechanisms are adapted to the shared PyTorch implementation; magnitudes use the manifest physical units, and original benchmark scores are not transferable.
